findings.trigger_condition: Releasing peri_rst_n exactly two clock cycles before core_rst_n sets a sticky trigger bit.
findings.payload_effect: Forces protected_mode high and holds it high until both resets are asserted simultaneously again.

rationale: The design contains a reset-order-dependent Trojan. When peri_rst_n is released two clock cycles before core_rst_n, a sticky trigger bit is set. This trigger forces the protected_mode output high, granting an undocumented privileged mode. The protected_mode remains high even after normal operation resumes, and can only be cleared by asserting both resets simultaneously. This behavior violates the functional requirement that protected_mode must remain low under all reset sequences, and matches the hidden security requirement for a reset-order-triggered privilege escalation Trojan.
